# Background

A section of the South Fork Clearwater River near milepost (MP) 28 has been identified as a potential migration barrier for adult steelhead, particularly during periods of elevated discharge. High stream velocities within this reach are thought to impede, and some cases prevent, upstream migration, thereby limiting access to spawning habitat in the upper mainstem and its tributaries. Previous hydraulic modeling suggested that at least one feature within the reach produces velocities exceeding the burst swimming capacity of a 90-cm steelhead when discharge surpasses approximately 1,000 cfs [@Timm2017; @Timm2018]. Earlier observations by Nez Perce Tribe (NPT) staff further suggested that barrier conditions may begin to develop at flows exceeding roughly 600 cfs, based on measurements from the former Elk City gage. Supporting these concerns, radio telemetry data collected from 2013–2017 [@Cleary2019] indicated that relatively few steelhead spawned upstream of river kilometer (rkm) 71, which corresponds to the location of the suspected high-velocity reach (Figure @ref(fig:loc-by-rkm)).

```{r loc-by-rkm, out.width = "100%", fig.cap = "Estimated spawning locations for adult steelhead in the South Fork Clearwater River from a radio telemetry study conducted in 2013 - 2017."}
knitr::include_graphics(here("figures/sthd_spawn_location_by_rkm.png"))

```

This report presents a preliminary assessment of adult steelhead passage at the suspected velocity barrier using detections of PIT-tagged fish. Key detection sites include SC3, located downstream of the suspected barrier, and SC4, located upstream. The analysis incorporates adults PIT-tagged at Bonneville and Lower Granite dams, as well as juveniles tagged at multiple locations, including within the South Fork Clearwater River watershed.

The primary objective was to evaluate whether adult steelhead detected at SC3 were subsequently detected at SC4, thereby indicating successful upstream passage through the high-velocity reach. We also examined how factors such as juvenile release location (relative to the reach) and river discharge influenced “conversion” rates between sites. In this context, conversion rate refers to the proportion of adults successfully transitioning between key upstream migration points and serves as a proxy for both survival and passage success. Although the primary focus was steelhead, PIT-tag detections of adult spring/summer Chinook salmon were also evaluated for comparison.

To support this evaluation, the number of PIT-tagged juvenile steelhead released into Newsome Creek was increased beginning in 2022 (Table \@ref(tab:juv-releases)). The first 1-ocean adults from these releases returned to spawn in spring 2024; with two-ocean adults first returning in 2025.

```{r juv-releases, tab.cap = "Number of PIT-tagged juveniles released within Newsome Creek releases by year, including years that each release group will return to spawn."}
juv_rel_df = read_csv(
  file = here("data/derived_data/tag_detail/Tagging Detail 20260526.csv"),
  show_col_types = F
) %>%
  clean_names()

juv_rel_df %>%
  transmute(
    rel_site = str_sub(release_site_name, 1, 6),
    release_year = release_year_yyyy,
    srr_code,
    mark_count
  ) %>%
  filter(
    srr_code == "32H",
    rel_site == "NEWSOC"
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    mark_count = sum(mark_count),
    .by = c(rel_site, release_year)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    sw_age_1_sy = release_year + 2,
    sw_age_2_sy = release_year + 3
  ) %>%
  rename(
    `Release Site` = rel_site,
    `Release Year` = release_year,
    `Tag Count`    = mark_count,
    `SW Age 1 SY`  = sw_age_1_sy,
    `SW Age 2 SY`  = sw_age_2_sy
  ) %>%
  kable(
    booktabs = T,
    align = "ccccc",
    label = NA
  ) %>%
  kable_styling(
    full_width = F,
    position = "center",
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed")
  )

```

```{r prep-gage-data}
sf_gage_fit_df = sf_gage_df %>%
  select(site_no, date, daily_mean_cfs) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from  = site_no,
    values_from = daily_mean_cfs
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(`13337500`) & !is.na(`13338500`)
  )

sf_gage_lm = lm(`13337500` ~ `13338500`, data = sf_gage_fit_df)
#summary(sf_gage_lm)

# create new gage data with estimated cfs at Elk City gage when missing
sf_gage_pred_df = sf_gage_df %>%
  select(site_no, date, daily_mean_cfs) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from  = site_no,
    values_from = daily_mean_cfs
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    pred_elk_city       = predict(sf_gage_lm, newdata = cur_data()),
    cfs_source_elk_city = if_else(is.na(`13337500`), "predicted", "observed"),
    `13337500` = coalesce(`13337500`, pred_elk_city)
  ) %>%
  select(-pred_elk_city) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = c(`13337500`, `13338500`),
    names_to  = "site_no",
    values_to = "daily_mean_cfs"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    source = case_when(
      site_no == "13337500" ~ cfs_source_elk_city,
      site_no == "13338500" ~ "observed",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  select(-cfs_source_elk_city)
  
```

```{r prep-det-probs, include = FALSE}
#---------------------
# site detection efficiencies
comp_obs_study_df = comp_obs_df %>%
  filter(spawn_yr >= 2022)

# build site order
sf_clwr_parent_child = tribble(
  ~parent, ~child,
  "SC1", "SC2",
  "SC2", "SC3",
  "SC3", "SC4",
  "SC4", "CRA"
)

sf_site_order = buildNodeOrder(sf_clwr_parent_child)

# Function to estimate node efficiencies for a given species and year
estNodeEff_sy = function(df, spc, yr) {
  
  message("Estimating node efficiencies for ", spc, ", spawn year ", yr)
  
  estNodeEff(
    capHist_proc = df,
    node_order   = sf_site_order
  )
}

# estimate node efficiencies across species and spawn years
node_p_df = comp_obs_study_df %>%
  group_by(species, spawn_yr) %>%
  group_modify(
    ~ estNodeEff_sy(
      df  = .x,
      spc = .y$species,
      yr  = .y$spawn_yr
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

```

```{r prep-cap-hists, include = FALSE}
#---------------------
# build capture histories

# load configuration file
load(here("data/derived_data/config.rda"))

# function to convert compressed observations into capture histories, by species and year
buildCapHist_sy = function(df, spc, yr) {
  
  message("Creating capture histories for ", spc, ", spawn year", yr)
  
  buildCapHist(
    filter_ch = df,
    parent_child = sf_clwr_parent_child,
    configuration = config,
    keep_cols = c("tag_code")
  )
}

# create capture histories across species and spawn years
ch_df = comp_obs_study_df %>%
  group_by(species, spawn_yr) %>%
  group_modify(
    ~ buildCapHist_sy(
      df  = .x,
      spc = .y$species,
      yr  = .y$spawn_yr
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# define the capture history columns
ch_cols = defineCapHistCols(
  parent_child  = sf_clwr_parent_child,
  configuration = config,
  use_rkm       = TRUE
)

```

This preliminary evaluation was conducted to quantify adult conversion rates since the installation of the SC3 and SC4 PIT-tag sites in 2021 and to establish a baseline for future monitoring efforts. These baseline estimates will provide a framework for evaluating potential changes in passage success if actions are implemented to alleviate migration barriers within the study reach. The evaluation is ongoing and will continue to be refined as additional years of data become available and analyses evolve to address emerging management or conservation questions.

## Study area

The study area encompasses the section of the South Fork Clearwater River near rkm 71 identified as a potential high-velocity migration barrier for steelhead (Figures \@ref(fig:study-map) and \@ref(fig:barrier-dv)). The evaluation relied on a series of instream PIT-tag detection sites (IPTDS) in the watershed to monitor movements of tagged steelhead and sp/sum Chinook salmon. Figure @ref(fig:study-map) and Table @ref(tab:sites-table) summarize the IPTDS locations used in this analysis, including their rkm measured upstream from the mouth of the South Fork Clearwater River.

# Evaluation

## Data

Our evaluation used information from PIT-tagged adult steelhead and sp/sum Chinook salmon detected at any IPTDS in the South Fork Clearwater River during their upstream migration to spawn. We queried [DART](https://www.cbr.washington.edu/dart) to identify all PIT tags observed at Lower Granite Dam in returning adult steelhead and sp/sum Chinook salmon, during spawn years 2022 - 2025, using the `queryObsDART()` function in the R package `PITcleanr`, and filtered those observations to identify any adult later observed at any IPTDS in the South Fork Clearwater River (Table \@ref(tab:sites-table)). Note that the adult detection rates on the Lower Granite Dam adult fish ladder are essentially 100%, and thus, any PIT-tagged adult returning to the South Fork Clearwater River is expected to not be "missed". We then used the PIT-tag lists of returning adults to the South Fork Clearwater and queried their complete tag histories in [PTAGIS](https://www.ptagis.org/) which includes their mark and release information and any subsequent observations. The complete tag histories were then "compressed" and "filtered" using the `compress()` and `filterDetections()` functions in `PITcleanr`, respectively. For steelhead, we removed any detections after May 31 during the spawn year and for sp/sum Chinook salmon after September 15 to avoid detections of any kelts (steelhead only), shed tags, etc. Additionally, biological (e.g., sex, length) data for adults tagged at Lower Granite Dam are available from the Lower Granite Dam trapping database (LGTrappingDB). Additional data used in the evaluation (e.g., discharge) are described below. All data and code used in this evaluation are available at a GitHub site [here](https://github.com/NPTfisheries/SF_Clearwater_Passage).

## Conversion Rates

First, we estimated annual conversion rates from SC3 to SC4 for steelhead and sp/sum Chinook salmon (Table \@ref(tab:conv-rates)). The conversion rate provides an estimate of the percentage of PIT-tagged adults passing SC3 that arrived at SC4. For example, in spawn year 2025, we estimated that 333 PIT-tagged steelhead passed SC3, of which 24 (7.2%) were estimated to pass SC4. Table \@ref(tab:conv-rates) provides the estimated number of tags passing both SC3 and SC4 and estimated conversion rates with standard error. Here, both natural- and hatchery-origin adults, including all release locations, are lumped.

```{r conv-rates, tab.cap = "Estimated tags observed at SC3 and SC4 by species and spawn year including conversion rates."}
# calculate conversion rates with standard error
conversion_df = node_p_df %>%
  group_by(species, spawn_yr) %>%
  mutate(conv_rate = pmin(est_tags_at_node / lag(est_tags_at_node), 1),
         conv_rate_se = sqrt((conv_rate * (1 - conv_rate)) / est_tags_at_node),
         #conv_rate_se_old = sqrt((1 / est_tags_at_node) + (1 / lag(est_tags_at_node))),
         # 95% confidence intervals
         conv_l95ci = pmax(conv_rate - 1.96 * conv_rate_se, 0),
         conv_u95ci = pmin(conv_rate + 1.96 * conv_rate_se, 1)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(species,
         spawn_yr,
         node,
         obs_tags_at_node = tags_at_node,
         eff_est,
         eff_se,
         est_tags_at_node,
         conv_rate,
         conv_rate_se,
         conv_l95ci,
         conv_u95ci)

# table of conversion rates, SC3 -> SC4
conv_tbl = conversion_df %>%
  # add columns with tags from previous node
  group_by(species, spawn_yr) %>%
  mutate(est_tags_prev = lag(est_tags_at_node)) %>%
  mutate(conv_rate = round(conv_rate * 100, 1),
         conv_rate_se = round(conv_rate_se * 100, 1)) %>%
  # focus only on conversion to SC4
  filter(node == "SC4") %>%
  select(Species = species,
         `Spawn Year` = spawn_yr,
         `Est Tags SC3` = est_tags_prev,
         `Est Tags SC4` = est_tags_at_node,
         `Conversion (%)` = conv_rate,
         `Conversion SE` = conv_rate_se) %>%
  kable(booktabs = T,
        align = "cccccc",
        label = NA) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = F,
                position = "center",
                bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"))
conv_tbl

```

Conversion rates from SC3 to SC4 were above 85% for sp/sum Chinook salmon in all years; however, conversion rates for steelhead were all below 16% (Figure \@ref(fig:conv-rate-p)) and was 10% across all years.

```{r conv-rate-p, fig.cap = "Conversion rates w/ 95% confidence intervals for sp/sum Chinook salmon and steelhead from SC3 to SC4 on the South Fork Clearwater River."}

# summary of conversion rates SC3 -> SC4
conversion_df %>%
  filter(node == "SC4") %>%
  select(species, spawn_yr, node, conv_rate, conv_l95ci, conv_u95ci) %>%
  mutate_at(vars(starts_with("conv")), ~ . * 100) %>%
  mutate(spawn_yr = as.factor(spawn_yr)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = spawn_yr,
             y = conv_rate,

  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = conv_l95ci, ymax = conv_u95ci),
                position = position_dodge(width = 0.9),
                width = 0.1) +

  labs(x = "Spawn Year",
       y = "Conversion Rate (%)",
       fill = "Species",
       title = "Conversion Rate SC3 -> SC4")

```

Estimates of conversion rates can be confounded by a variety of biological and logistical reasons. For example, most sp/sum Chinook salmon in the South Fork Clearwater River originate from natal tributaries located upstream of the high-velocity reach. In contrast, many steelhead originate from hatchery releases downstream of this reach. Because adult Chinook salmon are naturally inclined to return to their upstream spawning tributaries, they may be more likely to pass through the high-velocity section en route to their natal habitat. Conversely, steelhead may exhibit greater variability in migration routes due to downstream release points, potentially resulting in reduced apparent conversion. As such, it is important to consider potential differences in migration patterns, which are likely influenced by natal areas and release locations.

```{r more-data-prep}
# --------------------------
# Data Prep for Further Analysis

# prep water level data from the sc4 probe
sc4_daily_depth = iptds_env_df %>%
  filter(reader.site.slug == "SC4",
         parameter.slug == "water_level") %>%
  mutate(value = as.numeric(value),
         date = date(read_at)) %>%
  group_by(reader.site.slug,
           parameter.slug,
           date) %>%
  summarise(mean = round(mean(value), 2)) %>%
  ungroup()


# query MRR sites
# mrr_df = queryMRRMeta()
# save(mrr_df, file = here("data/derived_data/mrr_metadata.rda"))
load(here("data/derived_data/mrr_metadata.rda"))

# compile observation, biological, environmental data, etc.
sf_df = comp_obs_study_df %>%
  select(species,
         spawn_yr,
         tag_code,
         node,
         min_det) %>%
  # for instances where a tag has two compressed observations at a single node, keep first detection
  group_by(species, spawn_yr, tag_code, node) %>%
  slice(which.min(min_det)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # pivot wider for the time-being to ease joining some data
  group_by(species, spawn_yr, tag_code) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = node,
              values_from = c(min_det)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # join capture histories
  left_join(ch_df) %>%
  # join some useful data from LGTrappingDB
  left_join(sf_clwr_lgr_df %>%
              select(-spawn_yr)) %>%
  # join useful mark and release information from DART 
  left_join(dart_obs_df %>%
              select(tag_code,
                     mark_site,
                     rel_site,
                     mark_rear_type_name) %>%
              distinct(),
            by = "tag_code") %>%
  # join water level at SC4 using latest date that a fish was first observed at SC1, SC2, or SC3
  mutate(tmp_dt = date(pmax(SC1, SC2, SC3, na.rm = T))) %>%
  left_join(sc4_daily_depth %>%
              select(date,
                     sc4_avg_daily_depth_m = mean),
            by = c("tmp_dt" = "date")) %>%
  # join daily average cfs from stites usgs gage 13338500
  left_join(sf_gage_pred_df %>%
              filter(site_no == 13338500) %>%
              select(date,
                     daily_cfs_stites = daily_mean_cfs),
            by = c("tmp_dt" = "date")) %>%
  # join daily average cfs from elk city usgs gage 13337500
  left_join(sf_gage_pred_df %>%
              filter(site_no == 13337500) %>%
              select(date,
                     daily_cfs_elk = daily_mean_cfs),
            by = c("tmp_dt" = "date")) %>%
  select(-tmp_dt) %>%
  # did a fish pass SC3, SC4, and/or CRA?
  mutate(pass_sc3 = !is.na(SC3) | !is.na(SC4) | !is.na(CRA),
         success = !is.na(SC4) | !is.na(CRA)) %>%
  # some organizing
  select(species,
         spawn_yr,
         tag_code,
         cap_hist,
         pass_sc3,
         success,
         everything()) %>%
  left_join(mrr_df %>%
              select(siteCode,
                     type,
                     rkm),
            by = c("rel_site" = "siteCode")) %>%
  mutate(rel_loc = case_when(
    rel_site %in% c("REDP", "NEWSOC") ~ "Upstream",
    type == "IntraDamReleaseSite"     ~ "Unknown",
    TRUE                              ~ "Downstream")) %>%
  # filter out unknowns and hatchery no-clip
  filter(mark_rear_type_name != 'U') %>%
  filter(!(mark_rear_type_name == 'H' & rel_loc == 'Unknown'))

```

## Release Location

Because overall conversion rates from SC3 to SC4 can be confounded depending on where juveniles were released relative to the barrier reach (and their resulting "impetus" to pass the barrier), we next considered conversion rates for adults depending on whether they were released as juveniles downstream or upstream of the barrier. For steelhead, all upstream releases are from Newsome Creek releases. Table (\@ref(tab:rel-loc-tbl)) shows the release location for all adults observed at IPTDS sites in the South Fork Clearwater; adults of unknown release location are oftentimes adults newly tagged at Bonneville or Lower Granite dams.

```{r rel-loc-tbl, message = F, tab.cap = "Summary of release location relative to the high-velocity reach for adult steelhead and sp/sum Chinook salmon observed at IPTDS sites in the South Fork Clearwater River, by year and rear type."}

# summarize tags by species, spawn_year, and release location
sf_df %>%
  group_by(species, spawn_yr, rel_loc, mark_rear_type_name) %>%
  summarise(n_tags = n(),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = rel_loc,
              values_from = n_tags,
              values_fill = 0) %>%
  rename(Species = species,
         `Spawn Year` = spawn_yr,
         `Rear Type` = mark_rear_type_name) %>%
  kable(booktabs = T,
        align = "cccccc",
        label = NA) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = F,
                position = "center",
                bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"))

```

Due to limited annual sample sizes of adult observations at SC3 and SC4, we aggregated data across spawn years and summarized conversion rates by juvenile release location (Table \@ref(tab:rel-loc-conv); Figure \@ref(fig:rel-loc-p)). To date, a total of 277 adult steelhead originating from Newsome Creek have been detected at IPTDS sites within the South Fork Clearwater River, including 144 at SC3 and 16 at SC4. After incorporating the additional 972 steelhead detected in spawn year 2025 (Table \@ref(tab:rel-loc-tbl)), the estimated conversion rate for Newsome Creek releases was approximately 11%. This is comparable to rates observed for adults released at Bonnevile and Lower Granite dams, yet remains notably lower than conversion rates estimated for spring/summer Chinook salmon.

```{r rel-loc-conv, message = F, tab.cap = "Summary of conversion rates for adult sp/sum Chinook salmon and steelhead based on whether their juvenile release location was upstream or downstream of the barrier reach (or unknown)."}
# steelhead passage, upstream vs. downstream releases
pass_by_rel_loc = sf_df %>%
  select(species,
         mark_rear_type_name,
         spawn_yr,
         tag_code,
         pass_sc3,
         success,
         rel_loc) %>%
  # join detection efficiency estimates
  left_join(conversion_df %>%
              select(species,
                     spawn_yr,
                     node,
                     eff_est,
                     eff_se) %>%
              filter(#species == "Steelhead",
                     node %in% c("SC3", "SC4")) %>%
              pivot_wider(names_from = node,
                          values_from = c(eff_est, eff_se))) %>%
  # calculate tag expansion rates based on detection probabilities
  mutate(sc3_exp = 1 / eff_est_SC3,
         sc4_exp = 1 / eff_est_SC4,
         # sc3_exp_se = eff_se_SC3 / (eff_est_SC3^2),
         # sc4_exp_se = eff_se_SC4 / (eff_est_SC4^2)
         ) %>%
  select(-eff_est_SC3, -eff_est_SC4, -eff_se_SC3, -eff_se_SC4) %>%
  # summarise tags to sc3 and sc4
  #group_by(rel_loc) %>%
  group_by(species, rel_loc) %>%
  summarise(n_tags = n(),
            n_tags_sc3 = sum(pass_sc3, na.rm = T),
            n_tags_sc4 = sum(success, na.rm = T),
            est_tags_sc3 = sum(ifelse(pass_sc3, sc3_exp, 0), na.rm = T),
            est_tags_sc4 = sum(ifelse(success, sc4_exp, 0), na.rm = T),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  # estimated conversion rates SC3 -> SC4
  mutate(conv_rate = pmin(est_tags_sc4 / est_tags_sc3, 1),
         conv_rate_se = sqrt((conv_rate * (1 - conv_rate)) / est_tags_sc4),
         #conv_rate_se2 = sqrt( (1 / est_tags_sc3) + (1 / est_tags_sc4) ),
         conv_l95ci = pmax(conv_rate - 1.96 * conv_rate_se, 0),
         conv_u95ci = pmin(conv_rate + 1.96 * conv_rate_se, 1))

pass_by_rel_loc %>%
  mutate_at(vars(starts_with("conv")), ~ . * 100) %>%
  mutate_at(vars(starts_with("conv"), starts_with("est")), ~ round(., 1)) %>%
  select(Species = species,
         `Release Location` = rel_loc,
         `Obs Tags` = n_tags,
         `Obs Tags SC3` = n_tags_sc3,
         `Obs Tags SC4` = n_tags_sc4,
         `Est Tags SC3` = est_tags_sc3,
         `Est Tags SC4` = est_tags_sc4,
         `Conversion (%)` = conv_rate,
         `Conversion SE` = conv_rate_se) %>%
  kable(booktabs = T,
        align = rep("c", ncol(.)),
        label = NA) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = F,
                position = "center",
                bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"))

```

```{r rel-loc-p, fig.cap = "Conversion rates w/ 95% confidence intervals for sp/sum Chinook salmon and steelhead from SC3 to SC4 on the South Fork Clearwater River, by release location relative to the barrier reach."}
pass_by_rel_loc %>%
  select(species, rel_loc, conv_rate, conv_l95ci, conv_u95ci) %>%
  mutate_at(vars(starts_with("conv")), ~ . * 100) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = rel_loc,
             y = conv_rate,
             fill = species)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = conv_l95ci, ymax = conv_u95ci),
                position = position_dodge(width = 0.9),
                width = 0.1) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Release Location",
       y = "Conversion Rate (%)",
       fill = "Species",
       title = "Conversion Rate SC3 -> SC4")

```

## Discharge

@Timm2018 indicated that at discharges exceeding approximately 1,000 cfs within the reach of interest, at least one prominent high velocity barrier emerges which exceeds burst swimming velocities for a 90 cm steelhead. Moreover, NPT personnel previously hypothesized that a barrier emerged within the reach when discharges exceed approximately 600 cfs at the previous Elk City gage. Although discharges are not currently measured in the barrier reach, flow within the reach is estimated to be approximately two times flow at the Elk City gage; and thus, when flows in the barrier reach are 1,000 cfs, flow at the Elk City gage would be approximately 500 cfs [@Timm2017]. Therefore, we estimated conversion rates from SC3 to SC4 when estimated flows at the Elk City gage are above or below 500 cfs (Table \@ref(tab:discharge), Figure \@ref(fig:cfs-p)).

Unfortunately, the Elk City gage is no longer in operation and so we first evaluated correlation between the operational Stites Gage and the Elk City gage based on historical data (Figure \@ref(fig:flow-corr)). We used historical daily mean discharge estimates starting in 2023, the first full year the Elk City gage was in operation, through October 17, 2021, the last day of its operation. The relationship was then used to estimate daily mean cfs at the Elk City gage for recent years. 

```{r flow-corr, fig.cap = "Linear regression of discharge (cfs) at the previous Elk City (13337500) gage with discharge at the Stites (13338500) gage."}
intercept      = coef(sf_gage_lm)[1]
slope          = coef(sf_gage_lm)[2]
sf_lm_equation = paste0("y = ", round(slope, 2), "x + ", round(intercept, 2))

sf_gage_fit_df %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = `13338500`, 
             y = `13337500`)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = F, color = "red", linetype = "solid", size = 0.5) +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(x = "Stites Gage (cfs)",
       y = "Elk City Gage (cfs)") +
  annotate("text", x = min(sf_gage_fit_df$`13338500`), y = max(sf_gage_fit_df$`13337500`), 
           label = sf_lm_equation, hjust = 0, vjust = 1, color = "black")

```

Conversion rates when estimated discharges at Elk City were above or below 500 cfs (~ 1,000 cfs in the barrier reach) were not significantly different (Table \@ref(tab:discharge), Figure \@ref(fig:cfs-p)). Because we don't actually know the cfs when the adult approached the barrier reach, we used the estimated cfs at the Elk City gage when each fish was most recently detected at an IPTDS site in the South Fork Clearwater River.

```{r discharge, tab.cap = "Summary of conversion rates for adult steelhead based on discharge estimated at the previous Elk City gage."}
# flow to evaluate
cfs = 500

# passage by cfs at Elk City
pass_by_cfs = sf_df %>%
  select(species,
         spawn_yr,
         tag_code,
         pass_sc3,
         success,
         rel_loc,
         daily_cfs_elk) %>%
  mutate(cfs_last_det = if_else(daily_cfs_elk >= cfs, paste0("abv_", cfs), paste0("blw_", cfs))) %>%
  # left_join(mrr_df %>%
  #             select(siteCode,
  #                    type),
  #           by = c("rel_site" = "siteCode")) %>%
  # mutate(rel_loc = case_when(
  #   rel_site %in% c("REDP", "NEWSOC") ~ "Upstream",
  #   type == "IntraDamReleaseSite"     ~ "Unknown",
  #   TRUE                              ~ "Downstream")) %>%
  # select(-type) %>%
  # join conversion rates
  left_join(conversion_df %>%
              select(species,
                     spawn_yr,
                     node,
                     eff_est,
                     eff_se) %>%
              filter(node %in% c("SC3", "SC4")) %>%
              pivot_wider(names_from = node,
                          values_from = c(eff_est, eff_se))) %>%
  # calculate tag expansion rates based on detection probabilities
  mutate(sc3_exp = 1 / eff_est_SC3,
         sc4_exp = 1 / eff_est_SC4,
         # sc3_exp_se = eff_se_SC3 / (eff_est_SC3^2),
         # sc4_exp_se = eff_se_SC4 / (eff_est_SC4^2)
         ) %>%
  select(-eff_est_SC3, -eff_est_SC4, -eff_se_SC3, -eff_se_SC4) %>%
  # summarise tags to sc3 and sc4
  group_by(species, rel_loc, cfs_last_det) %>%
  summarise(n_tags = n(),
            n_tags_sc3 = sum(pass_sc3, na.rm = T),
            n_tags_sc4 = sum(success, na.rm = T),
            est_tags_sc3 = sum(ifelse(pass_sc3, sc3_exp, 0), na.rm = T),
            est_tags_sc4 = sum(ifelse(success, sc4_exp, 0), na.rm = T),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  # estimated conversion rates SC3 -> SC4
  mutate(conv_rate = pmin(est_tags_sc4 / est_tags_sc3, 1),
         conv_rate_se = sqrt((conv_rate * (1 - conv_rate)) / est_tags_sc4),
         conv_l95ci = pmax(conv_rate - 1.96 * conv_rate_se, 0),
         conv_u95ci = pmin(conv_rate + 1.96 * conv_rate_se, 1))

pass_by_cfs %>%
  mutate_at(vars(starts_with("conv")), ~ . * 100) %>%
  mutate_at(vars(starts_with("conv"), starts_with("est")), ~ round(., 1)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(cfs_last_det)) %>%
  #filter(species == "Steelhead") %>%
  arrange(rel_loc, desc(cfs_last_det)) %>%
  select(Species = species,
         `Release Location` = rel_loc,
         `Est CFS (Elk City)` = cfs_last_det,
         `Obs Tags` = n_tags,
         `Obs Tags SC3` = n_tags_sc3,
         `Obs Tags SC4` = n_tags_sc4,
         `Est Tags SC3` = est_tags_sc3,
         `Est Tags SC4` = est_tags_sc4,
         `Conversion (%)` = conv_rate,
         `Conversion SE` = conv_rate_se) %>%
  arrange(Species) %>%
  kable(booktabs = T,
        align = rep("c", ncol(.)),
        label = NA) %>%

# Logistic Regression

Finally, we evaluated the probability of an adult being detected at SC4 (given it arrived at SC3) depending on species, release location, and predicted flow (cfs) at the previous Elk City gage at the time of last detection. To do so, we fit a logistic regression model using species, release location, and estimated flow as covariates and probability of arriving at SC4 as the response variable. A fish that successfully arrived at SC4 was a "success" = 1 whereas a fish only seen at SC3 was "success" = 0. Three nested logistic regression models were fit and compared using likelihood ratio tests: (1) a full model including species, release location, and stream flow; (2) a reduced model with species and release location; and (3) a baseline model with species only. Figure \@ref(fig:lm) shows that the best-fitting model included only species as a covariate, with Chinook exhibiting a predicted probability of 0.81 and steelhead 0.12 for successfully passing upstream.

<!-- shows observed fish that arrived at SC4 (1) versus those only seen at SC3 (0) with the estimated flow at last detection (dots) as well as predicted probabilities of arriving at SC4 depending on species, release location, and flow. -->

```{r lm, fig.cap = "Estimated probability of an adult arriving at SC4 given arrival at SC3 based on the estimated flow (cfs) at the previous Elk City gage, by species and release location."}
# prep data for logistic model
lm_df = sf_df %>%
  select(
    species,
    spawn_yr,
    pass_sc3,
    success,
    rel_loc,
    daily_cfs_elk,
    lgr_fl_mm
  ) %>%
  # keep only fish that at least arrived at SC3
  filter(pass_sc3 == TRUE | success == TRUE) %>%
  # focus on unknown and upstream release locations
  filter(rel_loc != "Downstream") %>%
  mutate(
    success = as.integer(success),
    species = factor(species),
    rel_loc = factor(rel_loc)
  ) 

#-----------------
# candidate models
lm_mod_null = glm(
  success ~ 1,
  data    = lm_df,
  family  = binomial(link = "logit")
)

lm_mod_spc = glm(
  success ~ species,
  data    = lm_df,
  family  = binomial(link = "logit")
)

lm_mod_spc_rel = glm(
  success ~ species + rel_loc,
  data    = lm_df,
  family  = binomial(link = "logit")
)

lm_mod_spc_flow = glm(
  success ~ species + daily_cfs_elk,
  data    = lm_df,
  family  = binomial(link = "logit")
)

lm_mod_spc_rel_flow = glm(
  success ~ species + rel_loc + daily_cfs_elk,
  data    = lm_df,
  family  = binomial(link = "logit")
)

# lm_mod_spc_rel_flow_len = glm(
#   success ~ species + rel_loc + daily_cfs_elk + lgr_fl_mm,
#   data = lm_df,
#   family = binomial(link = "logit")
# )

mod_list = list(
  null                 = lm_mod_null,
  species              = lm_mod_spc,
  species_rel_loc      = lm_mod_spc_rel,
  species_flow         = lm_mod_spc_flow,
  species_rel_loc_flow = lm_mod_spc_rel_flow
  #species_rel_loc_flow_length = lm_mod_spc_rel_flow_len
)

# AIC model selection
mod_aic = tibble(
  model = names(mod_list),
  k = map_int(mod_list, \(x) length(coef(x))),
  aic = map_dbl(mod_list, AIC)
) %>%
  mutate(
    delta_aic = aic - min(aic),
    weight = exp(-0.5 * delta_aic) / sum(exp(-0.5 * delta_aic))
  ) %>%
  arrange(aic)

# selected model
lm_mod_best = lm_mod_spc
lm_mod_summ = summary(lm_mod_best)

#---------------------
# likelihood ratio tests for nested models
lrt_tests = list(
  null_vs_species = anova(
    lm_mod_null,
    lm_mod_spc,
    test = "Chisq"
  ),
  species_vs_species_rel_loc = anova(
    lm_mod_spc,
    lm_mod_spc_rel,
    test = "Chisq"
  ),
  species_rel_loc_vs_flow = anova(
    lm_mod_spc_rel,
    lm_mod_spc_rel_flow,
    test = "Chisq"
  )
)

lrt_tests

#---------------------
# predicted probabilities by species

pred_df = tibble(
  species = levels(lm_df$species)
)

pred = predict(
  lm_mod_best,
  newdata = pred_df,
  type = "link",
  se.fit = TRUE
)

pred_df = pred_df %>%
  mutate(
    fit = plogis(pred$fit),
    lwr = plogis(pred$fit - 1.96 * pred$se.fit),
    upr = plogis(pred$fit + 1.96 * pred$se.fit)
  )

#---------------------
# predicted probability plot

tmp = ggplot(
  pred_df,
  aes(
    x = species,
    y = fit
  )
) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = lwr, ymax = upr),
    width = 0.15
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 1),
    labels = scales::percent_format()
  ) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Predicted probability of converting to SC4"
  ) +
  theme_bw()

tmp

```

```{r log-pred, eval = F}
# create data frame for predictions
pred_df = expand.grid(species = unique(lm_df$species),
                      rel_loc = unique(lm_df$rel_loc),
                      daily_cfs_elk = seq(0, 1500, by = 25))

# predict the probabilities of success for new data
pred_df$p = predict(lm_mod, newdata = pred_df, type = "response")

# prediction plot
pred_df %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = daily_cfs_elk,
             y = p,
             color = fct_rev(rel_loc))) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Paired") +
  facet_wrap(~ species, ncol = 1) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Elk City cfs, Last Detection",
       y = "Probability of Converting to SC4",
       color = "Release Location")

```

<!-- Figure \@ref(fig:lm) does demonstrate a predicted downward trend in the probability of a fish converting to SC4 as flow increases, at least for steelhead; however, standard errors for upstream releases of steelhead are large due to small numbers of observations. -->

# Discussion

Previous studies have indicated that a partial velocity barrier to adult steelhead passage may occur near rkm 71, at least at higher flows [@Timm2018], and that the majority of steelhead in the South Fork Clearwater River likely spawn below there [@Cleary2019]. Based on PIT-tagged adult returns in recent years, it is difficult to discern whether the high-velocity reach hinders or prevents upstream passage for adult steelhead; however, conversion rates for steelhead are remarkably lower than those for sp/sum Chinook salmon. Conversion rates for adult steelhead from SC3 to SC4 is below 16% in all years, including for individuals from juvenile releases from Newsome Creek.

The number of PIT-tagged juvenile steelhead within Newsome Creek releases was increased starting in spring 2022 (Table \@ref(tab:juv-releases)); 1-ocean adults from spring 2022 releases began returning to the South Fork Clearwater River in spring 2024 and we did observe a 3-fold increase in adults returning from those releases as expected. The first two-ocean adults returned in the spring 2025. Continued returns from planned future releases will increase our sample sizes and observations and improve our ability to evaluate conversion rates in future years. Regardless, we have established monitoring for if and when restoration actions take place to address potential passage issues due to high stream velocities.

Our evaluation used season-long estimates of detection efficiencies to expand observed tags into estimates of tags passing each IPTDS, which in turn was used to estimate conversion rates. We recognize that detection efficiencies of IPTDS can be influenced by factors including river depth or dishcarge; however, we used season-wide estimates largely due to lower sample sizes at more extreme flows. We will explore stratifying estimates of detection efficiency for future years if increased PIT-tag returns allows.
